- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust upward by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.2) or volatile, model often over-forecasts; reduce forecast by 1–4% to align with mean reversion.  
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +2–3% above peak or use 3-period moving average.  
- If 3–5 consecutive forecast days show downward trend, model often fails to reverse; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias if sentiment turns positive.  
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to lag true price by 1–3 days; apply 1–2% upward correction if sentiment is bullish or volatility is rising.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.8, 0.2, 0.8), model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast with 3-period weighted average.  
- When true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% for 2+ consecutive days, model is under-reacting to sentiment; increase forecast by 2–5% for next period.
